pr_title: Add number platform to Z-Wave JS
pr_body:

Add number platform to Z-wave JS integration to handle values that can't be handled by other platforms, starting with the MultiLevel Switch CC used by thermostats for setting the valve position.

Discussed in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/46907

Hey there @home-assistant/z-wave, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with an integration (`zwave_js`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L554) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

> Sorry for suggesting this... 😬 , since there's a number platform, do you think the discovery should go back to detecting specific classes as lights, and then defaulting to number as a last resort? Or are you still satisfied with the new default being a light?
> 
> Could this number platform be used to support Sound Switch devices until a new platform is created? The Aeotec Siren 6 support has been desired for a long time.

Ha! I was wondering the same thing. In fact I tested the number entity with my Aeotec Siren.
But we have an approved architecture decision to add siren support so this is next on my list ;-)

And yes, we may also fall back to number for all number values as well and leave light scheme as-is but we'll have to account for the fact that we have to keep updating the scheme to support all scenarios...
For example that Aeon Labs switch providing an outlet AND a color led.

So, what should we do ? Any preferences ?

1) Widen the light scheme so MultiLevel Switch falls back to light in any case.
2) Use number platform as fallback for all number values.
3) A combination of 1 and 2: prefer light for multilevel switch but number for other number values.

The current approach is 1

I'm OK with option 1. It was trending that way anyways;  we have added almost all combinations of generic/specific device types that it has practically become a catch-all.

> Use number platform as fallback for all number values.

When you say this, do you mean any value, not even considering the Command Class?

> I'm OK with option 1. It was trending that way anyways; we have added almost all combinations of generic/specific device types that it has practically become a catch-all.
> 
> > Use number platform as fallback for all number values.
> 
> When you say this, do you mean any value, not even considering the Command Class?

OK, I'll leave it as-is.
Yes that's what I meant but atm I have no clue what other values are out there that might need the number platform.
The Sound Switch CC is a good candidate but that gets it own platform (siren) soon.

As an example, configuration parameter values can be numbers. Using the number platform for those would be interesting, as there was some interest in making them entities, and they would be both readable and writable as compared to a sensor. Maybe not a good idea though, some have states and cannot use a range of values, and we already have the service.

> configuration parameter values can be numbers

This is not the purpose of the number entity. Config is config, not a state.

> 
> 
> > configuration parameter values can be numbers
> 
> This is not the purpose of the number entity. Config is config, not a state.

I was referring to the values provided by node-zwave-js. Configuration parameter values can have the "number" type.

issue_context.title: Missing Manufacturer Specific mode and valve control for Aeotec TRV
issue_context.body:
## The problem
Currently, climate entity exposes only Heat and Off modes and three presets for Aeotec Thermostat Radiator Valve (ZWA021). 

However, Aeotec TRV supports a third mode, namely Manufacturer Specific, which allows direct valve control. Enabling this should expose a new entity (dimmer or cover type) allowing 0-100 / 0-255 valve control of the TRV.

When using Zwavejs2mqtt via mosquitto broker and mqtt integration, this third mode can be enabled by adding the following code in the ZWJS2M control panel - with fan_only: 31 being used to set the TRV to Manufacturer Specific

```
  "mode_map": {
    "off": 0,
    "auto": 1,
    "fan_only": 31

.......

  "discovery_payload": {
    "min_temp": 8,
    "max_temp": 28,
    "modes": [
      **"off",
      "auto",
      "fan_only"

........

    "mode_state_template": "{{ {0: \"off\",1: \"auto\",31: \"fan_only\"}[value_json.value] | default('off') }}",
```
This lets the user set the thermostat in Manufacturer Specific mode and control the valve position via a separate light dimmer entity. This allows to move the valve logic from the controller level up to HA level and allows the user to create more useful and precise automations for the TRV.

I know that the Zwave-js integration is at its beginning, but it would be useful if we could replicate this functionality via the Z-wave JS integration, without having to depend on a mqtt broker.

## Environment
HA core-2021.2.0b1 supervisor-2021.01.8 Z-Wave JS addon 0.1.1

Just further clarify, in open zwave beta these thermostats in my case the eurotronic spiritz enumerated with a valve position attribute that could be read in any mode.
The configuration of the device includes a parameter for setting the report period based on the %change of the valve.

And then in manufacturer specific mode that attribute becomes the only mechanism to set the valve %.

I use the valve % to calculate heat demand in my house, which in turn activates the boiler to provide the heat.

So it's going to be a little colder this week, and looking at the weather forecast it *is* going to be quite a bit cooler, with snow ❄️ on the weekend!

temp solution that's working for me is to get the valve position via MQTT. I'm doing this by: 
1. use zwavejs2mqtt, 
2. enable gateway/mqtt.
3. in home assistant:
```
- platform: mqtt
  name: "Lounge thermostat valve position"
  unit_of_measurement: "%"
  state_topic: "zwave/nodeID_33/38/0/currentValue"
  value_template: "{{ value_json.value }}"
```
